body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026 — a hot one, with highs near 103° and air quality at a moderate 64. Overnight, our city saw a shooting at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area, and we’re following the details. Grab your coffee and let’s catch up on the news.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. Officers broadcast an officer-safety alert and described the suspect as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Before that, around 2:16 a.m., crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street, where flames were visible inside a single-story structure with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire also drew a large response along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road, though crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries; the suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound. Other calls included a subject reported with a firearm in his waistband on Houchin Road, an assault on Birch Avenue in Wasco, a hit-and-run on Monterey Street involving a black Camry and a white sedan, two fire hydrants spilling water on 22nd Street between Q and P streets, about a half acre burning behind a residence on Windsong Street, a suspicious vehicle check on Culiacan Avenue, a family disturbance on Suncrest Drive involving an intoxicated teenager, a welfare check on a man lying on the ground near the curb on 26th Street, and an assault in progress with multiple people inside and a disturbance heard.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 64 — moderate.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon at the Capri Laundromat in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue.** Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Officers immediately provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim’s identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed. Anyone with information about this investigation is asked to call Detective Galvan or Detective Cazares at 661-792-2121.

**According to 23ABC, a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game left nearby residents shaken, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene.** The scene at Independence High School was chaotic as people tried to understand what had happened after gunshots rang out nearby. Erin Foster lives a few houses down from where the suspect was arrested. She said she was in shock when she learned what had happened. "I like our little neighborhood. That's kind of scary. I have, like, goosebumps. That's kind of scary. And he's 15. Oh, my." Foster said. Foster said she was on her way to her fiancé's workplace when she noticed an unusual scene outside her home. "We couldn't get out of the garage. There was, like, a little Hispanic family sitting over here on. I'm sorry, on the side of the garage, but there were a cop car in these undercover cars, and I was like, 'We can't get out.' So we had to ask him to move, but it was just odd 'cause then they were still here when I came back." Foster said. She said the family remained outside for an extended period of time. "Just odd that there was, like, a little Hispanic family, like a little baby, and like a mom it looked like, and some two, like, toddler little girls, and it was just like, 'Why are they sitting on the side of my garage?'" Foster said. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Eric Celedon said Friday night football games are safe and acknowledged why some community members may be hesitant to attend future games. "So we understand why someone would be fearful to come out, but we want to really reiterate.

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim’s family and friends and urged anyone with information about the shooting to contact the Bakersfield Police Department. She emphasized that the safety of our community is a top priority and that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. The mayor’s statement comes as the community grapples with the aftermath of the shooting, which has left many residents feeling unsafe and concerned about the safety of public events.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after the fatal shooting.** The event was scheduled to take place at the high school, but organizers decided to cancel it in light of the tragic incident. The cancellation is a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of attendees and to allow law enforcement to continue their investigation. The event was expected to feature local vendors, food trucks, and live music, but organizers say they plan to reschedule it for a later date.

## Something good

A local family is hosting a Saturday flea market to raise $8,900 for Villafana’s prosthetic leg. The event aims to support a community member in need of a prosthetic limb, and it’s a heartwarming example of neighbors coming together to help one of our own.

## Coming up this week

This week, the city council will hold a special meeting on Wednesday, August 26, at 12:00 p.m., followed by two regular city council meetings at 3:30 p.m. and 5:15 p.m. on the same day. On the cultural front, the Fox Theater will host a variety of events, including Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on Saturday, August 22; Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 on Tuesday, August 25; Rodney Carrington on Thursday, August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 28; Willie Barcena on Saturday, August 29; and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on Saturday, August 29. Be sure to check the schedules and plan accordingly.
